title: When volunteer mobilization outpaces coordination: workflow repair in disaster response
journal: Disaster Prevention and Management: An International Journal
abstract: Purpose This study examines what happens when rapid volunteer mobilization expands faster than the capacity to organize heterogeneous people, information, resources and tasks during disaster response. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a single embedded qualitative process design centered on a rapidly scaled, messaging-mediated volunteer response following a September 2025 barrier-lake flood in eastern Taiwan. The primary process evidence consists of contemporaneous records from the focal coordination group, supplemented by targeted traces from task-specific subgroups, two public forums, nine semi-structured interviews, five fieldnote-based observations and open-ended volunteer accounts. Findings Mobilization-generated coordination strain became visible through repeated verification, misrouting, uneven task allocation, stale or ambiguous requests and situations in which volunteers or resources accumulated in some locations while remaining needed elsewhere. The analysis identifies three recurrent forms of workflow repair: functional differentiation, boundary regulation and intermediary translation. These practices were observably enacted and reused, but repair remained partial, uneven and subject to changing task demand, participant learning, formal intervention and safety constraints. Originality/value The study distinguishes the capacity to mobilize help from the capacity to organize what has been mobilized. It conceptualizes workflow repair as an episode-level, problem-triggered process linking an identifiable coordination breakdown to targeted reconfiguration of an already operating workflow, observable uptake or reuse and a bounded process consequence or incomplete repair after volunteer mobilization has already scaled.

title: When does AI dependence for decisions trigger moral disengagement? A proposed model with ethical position as a moderator
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to present a conceptual model investigating the moderating role of individuals’ ethical positions (idealism and relativism) in the relationship between dependence on artificial intelligence (AI) for decisions and moral disengagement. Design/methodology/approach Theoretical explanations and logical connections among the variables are developed within a propositional framework by integrating conservation of resources theory, social cognitive theory and ethics position theory, informed by research on algorithmic decision-making and moral disengagement. Findings This study proposes that dependence on AI for decisions is positively associated with moral disengagement. Idealism is expected to weaken this relationship, whereas relativism is expected to strengthen it where organisational performance demands favour accepting AI recommendations despite foreseeable stakeholder harm. The model concerns employees who retain meaningful discretion over AI-supported decisions. Practical implications Organisations should provide meaningful opportunities to question and escalate AI recommendations and examine whether performance expectations discourage ethical review. Training should address stakeholder harm and responsibility-displacing rationalisations. Originality/value This study distinguishes dependence on AI for decisions from general AI usage and restrictions on employee autonomy. It develops an explanation of how such dependence may facilitate moral disengagement and identifies idealism and relativism as distinct boundary conditions, specifying the context of the proposed strengthening effect of relativism.

title: Viewpoint: understanding consumer vulnerability across service ecosystem configurations
abstract: Purpose This viewpoint aims to advance understanding of consumer vulnerability by examining how different configurations of structural, institutional and relational conditions shape vulnerability across service ecosystems. Country context, regulation and customer-to-customer (C2C) interaction provide complementary perspectives for examining these conditions. Design/methodology/approach This paper adopts a conceptual, integrative approach, synthesising literature from transformative service research, service ecosystem theory and marketing to develop an analytical framework that integrates country context, regulation and C2C interaction. Findings Consumer vulnerability varies according to the configuration and interdependence of structural conditions, institutional arrangements and relational processes. Together, these conditions may create, reinforce, negotiate or alleviate vulnerability across different service ecosystems. Research limitations/implications The framework encourages comparative, multi-level and longitudinal research examining how structural, institutional and relational conditions combine and change across service ecosystem configurations. Practical implications The framework encourages service providers and policymakers to adopt ecosystem-oriented strategies that consider structural, institutional and relational conditions together when addressing sources of vulnerability. Originality/value Building on existing understandings of vulnerability as dynamic and ecosystem-based, this viewpoint provides an analytical framework for explaining how variation and interdependence among structural, institutional and relational conditions shape vulnerability across service ecosystems, supporting more comparative and context-sensitive theorising within TSR.

title: UNIFORM RULES IN THE FIELD OF CONSUMER RIGHTS PROTECTION: ON THEIR PLACE IN THE SYSTEM OF RUSSIAN LEGISLATION AND KEY NOVELTIES. PART 2
abstract: The article analyzes the innovations in the field of consumer protection legislation that arose in connection with the approval, by Decree of the Supreme State Council of the Union State, of the Uniform Rules in the Field of Consumer Protection, which came into force on December 6, 2024, on the territory of the Russian Federation and the Republic of Belarus. The article analyzes the main changes introduced by this act into Russian legislation, noting the focus of the Uniform Rules on raising the level of guarantees of consumer rights and interests, imposing additional obligations on business entities, expanding the scope of application to relations arising from the acquisition of goods, works, and services on a gratuitous basis, as well as the involvement of persons who do not have the status of individual entrepreneurs and sell their products to consumers.

title: Threshold-based multi-scale analysis of thermal-acoustic comfort in urban public spaces: identifying critical thresholds and individual heterogeneity
The volatility spillover between digital currencies and stock markets:evidence from DCC-GARCH R2 decomposed connectedness measures
abstract: Abstract Based on weekly data from December 2018 to October 2025, this study employs the DCC-GARCH R² decomposed connectedness approach to investigate volatility spillovers between four major digital currencies (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tether USD, USD Coin) and five key stock markets (China, the U.S., Germany, Japan, and the UK). Empirical findings reveal three core insights. First, dynamic conditional correlations exhibit distinct patterns across digital currency subtypes and stock markets: public chain coins (BTC and ETH) are strongly correlated with each other, stablecoins show negative correlations with other assets, and China’s stock market remains largely insulated from global markets. Second, R² decomposed connectedness analysis reveals substantial cross-market linkages, with China’s stock market displaying the weakest connectedness and the U.S. market acting as the primary risk transmitter. Third, the dynamic total connectedness index exhibits three distinct peaks in early 2019, the first half of 2020, and mid-2023, before entering a current downward trajectory. These peak periods may be associated with possible explanations, including the 2019 crypto crash, the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic, and the 2023 regulatory changes. Net connectedness analysis identifies BTC, the U.S., and German markets as net transmitters of shocks, while China, Japan, and the UK are net receivers. These findings underscore the heterogeneous spillover dynamics across digital currency subtypes, offering actionable insights for cross-market risk management and asset allocation.

title: The impact of increased child benefits on tempo and quantum of fertility in Estonia
Strengthening the diagnosis of death due to lightning: an integrated forensic approach – a literature review
abstract: Abstract The diagnosis of “death by lightning strike” is typically confirmed through an external postmortem examination. The principle pathological findings are typically located on the external aspects of the body and clothing, while internal examination typically reveals few, if any, specific or diagnostic pathological changes. Following a fatal lightning strike, the victim may have only subtle or no typical findings on the body’s surface. Misdiagnoses have occurred repeatedly in the past. Therefore, this literature review investigated whether autopsies of lightning strike victims can lead to or support the correct diagnosis. From a total of 120 case reports on lightning strike accidents with autopsy findings, 34 cases exhibited characteristic injuries that the authors attributed to the lightning strike. The head, heart, lungs, and skeletal system were the most commonly affected areas. Since there is currently no pathognomonic finding for internal injuries after a lightning strike incident, the authors propose at least one additional piece of evidence in addition to a characteristic finding to establish the correct diagnosis. The diagnostic certainty of a lightning-related death may be increased by corroborative evidence, which may include reliable witness accounts, additional trace evidence indicative of a lightning strike at the location where the body was found, or confirmation of lightning activity in the area by a regional lightning detection system.

title: Regional digital finance and food supply-chain management resilience: evidence on the regional-to-firm conversion gap in China’s emerging listed food enterprises
abstract: Food supply chains face climate shocks, logistics disruption, food-safety incidents and volatile demand, yet the relevance of regional digital finance for firm-level resilience remains uncertain. This study examines the association between a province-level digital-finance environment and an accounting-based food supply-chain resilience proxy among emerging listed food enterprises in China. Using public data for 122 eligible firms, we construct annual resistance, recovery and stability measures from revenue, operating cash flow and net margin; the common two-way fixed-effects sample contains 732 firm-year observations from 119 firms during 2017–2023. Regional digital finance is measured as a province-level external financial environment rather than firm-level digital transformation or adoption. Operational capability and regional consumption capacity are accounting- and province-level proxies and do not directly observe supplier coordination, traceability, cold-chain performance, or product-level demand. The preferred estimate is close to zero [beta = −0.005, SE = 0.063, 95% CI (−0.128, 0.117)]. Alternative covariance estimators, outcome definitions and timing specifications do not establish a stable positive within-firm association. The proxy-based operational-capability pathway and the conditional consumption-capacity association are likewise not established. Equivalence tests at 0.05 and 0.10 SCR-standard-deviation bounds are not significant, and the approximate 80% minimum detectable effect is 1.575 SCR standard deviations. The evidence therefore cannot distinguish a small contextual association from limited within-firm statistical precision. The findings support a bounded regional-to-firm conversion interpretation: regional finance may widen resource availability, but whether it is associated with resilience depends on unobserved operational conversion routines and food-sector coordination conditions.
